title: Jiuzhang photonic quantum advantage
summary: Gaussian boson sampling experiments that first claimed quantum advantage in China.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

The Jiuzhang series, from the University of Science and Technology of China, used squeezed light and interferometers to perform Gaussian boson sampling faster than classical simulation. The 2023 iteration reported 255 detected photons. These machines solve a narrow sampling problem and are not programmable general-purpose computers, a distinction often lost in coverage.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2020–2028
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

  • China's 15th Five-Year Plan

Investment Exposure

Photonic advantage claims should be read as physics results, not as progress toward useful computation.

What Would Change The View

  • Independent verification of advantage claims.
  • Error rates and programmability.
  • Commercial applications beyond sampling.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
